en: Having bowed to the Supreme Person, the God born from the navel of the Best of Men, I shall speak the lexicon named *Pāiyalacchī*; listen! *PāiLaNā.1*:
Kamalāsana, Svayambhū, Pitāmaha, Caturmukha, and Parameṣṭhin [are names for Brahmā].
The Elder [is] Viṣṇu, Viriñca, the Lord of Creatures, and the one born from the lotus.
Dakṣāyaṇī, Bhavānī, the Daughter of the Mountain, Pārvatī, Umā, Gaurī, Āryā, Durgā, Kālī, Śivā, and Kātyāyanī, Caṇḍī.
The sun is called *akkō*, *taraṇī*, *mittō*, *mattaṇḍō*, *diṇamaṇī*, *payaṅgō*, *ahimayarō*, *paccūhō*, *diyasarō*, and *aṁsumālī*.
The moon is called *indū*, *nisāyarō*, *sasaharō*, *vihū*, *gahavaī*, and *rayaṇināhō*. (PāiLaNā.4)
The moon is known as Mayalañchaṇa (the deer-marked), Himayara (the snow-mountain), Rohiṇiramaṇa (the lover of Rohiṇī), Sasi (the cool-rayed), and Canda (the bright).
Fire is known as Dhūmaddhaya (smoke-bannered), Huyavaha (oblation-bearer),

Vihāvasu (the radiant), Pāvaka (the purifier), Sihī (the lion-like), Vaṇhī (the burner), Aṇala (the windless), Jalaṇa (the consumer), Ḍahana (the burner), Huyāsaṇa (the oblation-eater), and Havvavāha (the carrier of the offering).
Mayaraddha, Anaṅga, Raïṇāha, Vammaha, Kusumabāṇa,
Kandappa, Pañcasara, Mayaṇa, and Saṅkappajoṇī are synonyms for Love (Kāma).
Mayarahara, Sindhuvaī, Sindhū, Rayaṇāyara, and Salilarāsī are synonyms for the ocean.
The ocean is pārāvāra, jaladhi, taraṅgamālī, and samudra. (PāiLaNā.
8) An elephant is called pīlu, gaja, mayagala, māyaṅga, sindhura, kareṇu, doghaṭṭa, dantī, vāraṇa, karī, kuñjara, and hastī. (PāiLaNā. 9)

Amburuha, sayavatta, saro-ruha, puṇḍarīya, aravinda, rāīva, tāmarasa, mahuppala, paṅkaya, and naliṇa are synonyms for the lotus. Phullaṇḍuha, rasāū, bhiṅga, bhasala, mahuyara, and aliṇa are synonyms for the bee. *Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā* 10.2–3.
*Indindirā*, *durehā*, *dhuyagāyā*, *chappayā*, and *bhamarā* are words for a bee.
(PāiLaNā.11) *Rāmā*, *ramaṇī*, *sīmantiṇī*, *vahū*, *vāmalōyaṇā*, *vilayā*, *mahilā*, *juvaī*, *abalā*, *niyambinī*, *aṅgaṇā*, and *nārī* are words for a woman. (PāiLaNā.12)
Those who follow their own desires are unrestrained, unbridled, liberated,
free from fetters, without support, self-willed, unchecked, and lacking self-control.
(PāiLaNā.13) [They pursue that which is] delightful, pleasant, charming, lovely, beautiful, and attractive.
*Laṭṭhaṃ*, *kantaṃ*, *suhayaṃ*, *manōramaṃ*, *cāru*, and *ramaṇijjaṃ*.
*Masiṇaṃ*, *saṇiyaṃ*, *maṭṭhaṃ*, *mandaṃ*, *alasaṃ*, *jaḍaṃ*, *marālaṃ*,
*khēlaṃ*, *nihuaṃ*, *saïraṃ*, *vīsatthaṃ*, *mantharaṃ*, and *thimiyaṃ*.
Know that it is kindled, set ablaze, ignited, and set on fire;
it is whirled about, raised up, tossed upward, and made to blaze forth;
[it is] instantly, immediately, quickly, suddenly, and all at once.
It is not left unoccupied, it is solitary, unexpected, and sudden.
A multitude, a crowd, a confusion, a throng, a mass, a host, a collection, a flock, a company, a gathering, a swarm, a group, a heap, and a cluster. (PāiLaNā.18)

In this section, we shall describe the synonyms for the state of liberation—namely Sandoha, Nīrāmbu, Bhara, Nihāya, and Samūha—by means of these half-verses regarding the nature of the subject matter.
(PāiLaNā. 19) The summit of the world, the supreme state, liberation, perfection, auspiciousness, and nirvāṇa.
Śuddhōdayanī, Daśabala, Śakra, Sugata, Jina, Buddha; Śaurī, Daśārhanātha, Vaikuṇṭha, Mahumaha, Uvinda, Sūlī, Śiva, Piṇāī, Thāṇu, Giriśa, Bhava, Sambhu. (PāiLaNā. 20–21)
Kañcārī, Khaṇḍa, Chaṁmuha, Visāha, Guha, Kumāra, Amara, Tiyasa, Vandāraya, Vibuha, Sura, and Deva;
Akkhaṇḍala, Suravaī, Purandara, Vāsava, and Suṇāsīra. (PāiLaNā. 22)
Rāma, Śrī, Musalāyudha, Bala, and Kāmapāla;
Peyāhiya, Kayanta, Kīnāsa, Antaka, Yama, Kāla, Vessamaṇa, Nihināha, and Kubera, the lord of the Yakṣas. (PāiLaNā 23–24)
Aṇila, gandhavaha, māruya, samīra, pahañjana, pavaṇa, vinayasua, khayaraa, takkha, pannagariu, garula; uraa, ahī,
bhuyaṅga, bhuyaṅgama, pannaa, phaṇī, bhuyaō.
The Daityas, Dānavas, Asuras, and Surāri-s are enemies of the gods.
(PāiLaNā.26) Abhra, dhūmayoni, balāhaka, jaladhara, and jīmūta are synonyms for cloud.
Kha, abhra, antarikṣa, vyoman, naha, ambara, and gagana are synonyms for the sky. (PāiLaNā.27)

Ambu, salilaṃ, vaṇaṃ, vāri, nīraṃ, udayaṃ, dayaṃ, payaṃ, tōyaṃ, sariyā, taraṅgiṇī, niṇṇayā, naī, āvayā, sindhū; vasuhā, vasundharā, vasumaī, mahī, mēiṇī, dharā, dhariṇī. (PāiLaNā.28) Water: ambu, salilaṃ, vaṇaṃ, vāri, nīraṃ, udayaṃ, dayaṃ, payaṃ, tōyaṃ; river: sariyā, taraṅgiṇī, niṇṇayā, naī, āvayā, sindhū. Earth: vasuhā, vasundharā, vasumaī, mahī, mēiṇī, dharā, dhariṇī.
The *abbhapisāya*, Rāhu, Gahakacchola, and Viḍappa;
[these are] the spirits (*bhūta*) such as the *ḍhayara*, *puya*, *pippaya*, *pareya*, *sallaya*, *rayaṇiyara*, *jāuha*, *kavvāya*, *koṇava*, and *rakkha*. (PāiLaNā 29–30)
The Mandākinī, the celestial river Gaṅgā, the Bhāgīrathī, and the daughter of Jahnu;
likewise, *mēha*, *mai*, *maṇīsā*, *vinnāṇaṃ*, *dhī*, *ciī*, and *buddhī*.
*Jaïṇō*, *tavassiṇō*, *tāvasā*, *risī*, *bhikkhuṇō*, *muṇī*, and *samaṇā*.
The auspicious verses were recited by the wandering bards and panegyrists. (PāiLaNā.32) *Āsa*, *satti*, *vāha*, *haya*, *turaṅga*, *turaṅgama*, and *tura* denote a horse;
*saṅgāma*, *sañjuya*, *āhava*, *raṇa*, *saṅgara*, and *samara* denote battle. (PāiLaNā.33)
*Rōla*, *rāva*, *vaya*, *halabola*, *kalayala*, *vamāla*, *senā*, *varūhinī*, *vāhinī*, *anīkaṃ*, *camū*, and *sinnam* [are synonyms for army].
(PāiLaNā 34) *Rora*, *akiñcana*, *duvviha*, *daridda*, *dugga*, and *nissa* [are synonyms for a pauper]. (PāiLaNā 34)
*Sattu* means enemy, adversary, foe, opponent, or rival.
*Kaṇaya*, *silīmukha*, *maggaṇa*, *isū*, *sāyaka*, *sara*, *visiha*, and *pakkha* mean arrow;
*samattha*, *pakkala*, *paccala*, and *poḍha* mean capable or strong. (Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā 35–36)
A *kōyaṇḍa*, a *gandīva*, a *dhamma*, a *dhaṇuha*, a *sarāsaṇa*, a *cāva*, a sword (*khagga*), a blade (*asī*), a scimitar (*kivāṇa*), a sabre (*karavāla*), and a round-headed sword (*maṇḍalagga*).
(PāiLaNā.37) A lion, frost, mist, dust, and a cloud of smoke.
Kallōla, ullōla, ummī, vīī, and taraṅga are synonyms for wave. (PāiLaNā.38) Know that *nīluppala*, *kuvalaya*, and *indīvara* refer to the blue lotus;
*kanduṭṭha*, *candujjaya*, *kumuya*, *gaddahaya*, *kērava*, and *sappha* refer to the white lotus. (PāiLaNā.39)
Dhayaraṭṭha, kāyaṃba, haṃsa, dhavala-sauṇa, marāla, saūla, saharā, mīṇa, timi, jhasa, and aṇimisa are types of fish;
saüṇa, khaga, saünta, pattaraha, aṇḍaya, and vihaṅga are types of birds. (PāiLaNā. 40)
Sāṇā, bhasaṇā, indamahakāmuyā, maṇḍalā, and kavilā.
(PāiLaNā.41) The female cuckoo is called piyamāhavī or parahuyā; the male cuckoo is the kalayaṇṭhī or kōilā.
The peacock is the vanasavāī, morā, sihi, barahiṇo, sihaṇḍiṇo, or nīlakaṇṭhā. (PāiLaNā.42)

Sāhāmao, balimuhō, pavaṅgamo, vāṇaro, kaī, pavaō, pañcāṇaṇō, mayārī, mayāhivō, kēsari, sīhō; baliuḍḍhā, riṭṭhā, vukkaṇā, vaḍhaṅkā, kāyalā, kāyā. (PāiLaNā. 43) Monkey, lion-faced, leaping, ape, monkey, tree-dweller, five-clawed, bear, lord of bears, maned one, lion; ruddy goose, rhinoceros, vulture, osprey, crane, body-born, body. (PāiLaNā. 43)
The *illī*, *pullī*, *vaggō*, *saddūlō*, and *puṇḍarīō*.
The *nandī*, *tambā*, *bahulā*, *giṭṭhī*, *mōlā*, *rōhiṇī*, *surahī*, *ēṇī*, *hariṇī*, *kamalā*, *mayī*, *kuraṅgī*, and *sāraṅgī*.
*Gosā*, *rayaṇivirāma*, *gosagga*, *diṇamuhā*, and *paccūsa* mean dawn;
*ghamma*, *tāva*, *ḍāha*, *umhā*, *uṇha*, and *nirōha* mean heat.
*Aṃsu*, *rassī*, *pāyā*, *karā*, *maūhā*, *gahatthiṇo*, and *kiraṇā* mean rays of light. (PāiLaNā 46)
*rayaṇī*, *vihāvarī*, *savvarī*, *nisā*, *jāmiṇī*, and *rāī* [mean] night.
*ālōo*, *ujjōo*, *dittī*, *bhāsā*, *pahā*, and *payāsō* mean light;
while *santamasam*, *andhayāraṁ*, *dhantaṁ*, *timiraṁ*, and *tamissaṁ* mean darkness.
House, dwelling, abode, residence, shelter, home, mansion, wealth, riches, property, essence, fortune, assets, treasure, and substance;
mountain, rock, stone, peak, great earth-bearer, supporter, and peaked mountain. (PāiLaNā 49)
Gold, *kaṇaya*, *cāmīyara*, *pasiṇḍi*,
and *tavaṇijja*. Speech, *vāṇī*, *vāyā*, *bhaṇiī*, *sarassaī*, *bhāraī*, *girā*, *bhāsā*, *āyaṅkō*,
*āyallō*, *vāhī*, as well as *āmaō* and *rōhō*.
*Magga*, *pantha*, *saraṇī*, *addhāna*, *vattiṇī*, *paha*, *payavī*, *uttaṃsa*, *avayaṃsa*, *kaṇṇelī*, and *kaṇṇūrō* are [synonyms for] road (*patha*).
(PāiLaNā 52) *Duriya*, *kalusa*, *dukkaḍa*, *ahaṃ*, *adhamma*, and *kamma* are [synonyms for] evil action (*pāpa*). (PāiLaNā 52)
Falsehood, delusion, futility, untruth, and that which is unreal.
*Sāhī*, *viḍavī*, *vaccha*, *mahīruha*, *pāyava*, *duma*, and *taru* are synonyms for tree;
likewise, *kuñjala*, *kumpala*, *kōraya*, and *chāraya* denote a bud. (PāiLaNā 53–54)
*Avalepa*, *ahaṃkāra*, *mada*, *maratta*, *maḍapphara*,
*dappa*, *uppēhaḍa*, *uḍḍāmara*, *ubbhaḍa*, and *āḍambarilla* are synonyms for pride.
(PāiLaNā 55) *Abhisāriyā*, *aḍayaṇā*, *paṃsulī*, *chiñchaī*, and *dussīlā* are synonyms for a woman of ill-repute.
*Jāyā*, *pattī*, *dārā*, *ghariṇī*, *bhajjā*, and *purandhī* are terms for wife.
*Kabarī*, *kuntalahāra*, *dhammilla*, *kesahatthao*, *mauḍī*, *cūlā*, *sihā*, *sihaṇḍī*, *siṃhaliyā*, *chiṇḍao*, and *caḍao* refer to the hair or its arrangement. (Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā 56–57)

A young one, a child, a small one, a babe, a tender infant, a youth, a servant-girl, a little girl, and a child with a mouth smelling of milk; [these are synonyms for a child]. Body, limb, frame, constitution, form, person, and self; [these are synonyms for the body]. *Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā* 58.
*Duī*, *biijja*, *aṇuyara*, *sahāya*, and *sahayara*.
*Caūra*, *niuṇa*, *kusala*, *chēya*, *viusa*, *buhā*, *pattaṭṭha*, *maṇuya*, *nara*, *maṇussa*, *maccā*, as well as *māṇava* and *purisa*. (PāiLaNā. 59–60)
Know that *vacchīutta*, *caṇḍila*, *ṇhāviya*,
*rattīya*, *ramaṇa*, *kanta*, *paṇaī*, *pāṇasama*, *piyayama*, and *daïa* all mean "lover.
*Vicchaḍḍa*, *sāmiddhi*, *ridḍhi*, *vihava*, *sirī*, and *sampatti* all mean "prosperity."
*juyala* (pair), *juya* (yoke), *juyāṇa* (youth), *puyaṇḍa* (blossom), *bōdraha* (tree), *taruṇa* (young).
*vivara* (cavity), *kuhara* (hollow), *randha* (hole), *kucchilla* (crooked), *antara* (interval), *kuḍilla* (curved);
*ōlī*, *mālā*, *rāī*, *riñchōlī*, *āvalī*, *pantī* (all meaning row or line).
Maireya, madhvāra, sihu, sara, madhu, avakarasa,
kāyambharī, prasannā, hālā, as well as vāruṇī and maireya—
these are terrible, fierce, radiant, formidable, intoxicating, fearsome, and terrifying. (PāiLaNā 64)
Ill-trained, fierce, fickle, and unrefined;
*vāulla*, *jambulla*, *muhula*, and *bahujampira*; *vāyāla*, *vuttanta*, *uyanta*, and *vatta*—these are names for a talkative person (*paüttināmāï*). (PāiLaNā 65–66)
*Kāla*, *velā*, *samaya*, *prastāva*, *antara*, and *avasara* are synonyms for time;
likewise, *iha*, *ihaī*, *sampaī*, *iṇhiṃ*, *ittāhē*, *sampayaṃ*, *dāṇiṃ*, and *dāṇim* [are synonyms for "now"].
(Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā 67) *Cindhā*, *vējayantī*, *paḍāyā*, *kēuṇa*, *dhaya*, and *huḍuma* are synonyms for a banner.
Kuppāsa, kañcuya, gindhulla, and vāravāṇa;
jāṇa, sicaya, kaḍilla, niyaṃsaṇa, sāhulī, parihaṇaya, cēla, vāsa, vasaṇa, aṃsuya, ambara, and vattha—these are synonyms for clothing. (PāiLaNā 68–69)
Ease, charm, playfulness, splendor, grace,
sportiveness, effort, desire, longing, faith, passion, and hope.
Childish, deluded, dull, ignorant, foolish, inert, and stupid.
Pāmara, gahavaï, sēyāla, kāsayā, dōṇaya, and haliya;
poraccha, pisuṇa, maccharī, khala, muhumuha, upphāla, kamala, kusumāla, takkara, pāḍaccara, and thēṇa. (PāiLaNā 71–72)

*niḍdhaṃdhā*, *nisaṃsā*, *niccuḍḍā*, *nikkivā*, *akaruṇā*, *ya*, *ruṃdā*, *pīṇā*, *thūlā*, *ya*, *maṃsalā*, *pīvarā*, *thōrā*. *Sarisō*, *samō*, *saricchō*, *saṅkāsō*, *sacchahō*, *samāṇō*, *ya*. (PāiLaNā 73) [The following are synonyms for "lazy": *niḍdhaṃdhā*, *nisaṃsā*, *niccuḍḍā*, *nikkivā*, *akaruṇā*, *ruṃdā*, *pīṇā*, *thūlā*, *maṃsalā*, *pīvarā*, *thōrā*. [The following are synonyms for "equal": *sarisō*, *samō*, *saricchō*, *saṅkāsō*, *sacchahō*, *samāṇō*, *ya*.
Hard, harsh, cruel, rough, gnawing, and severe;
flat-nosed, flat, thin, stubborn, arrogant, and fierce; fickle, longing, eager, greedy, and lustful. (PāiLaNā 74–75)

*Saṇṇaṃ*, *khinnaṃ*, *suṭṭhiyaṃ*, *uvvāyaṃ*, *nīsahaṃ*, *kilantaṃ*, *ca*, *āiggaṃ*, *uvviggaṃ*, *uccēyaṃ*, *vuṇṇaṃ*, *uttatthaṃ*. *Ghaḍiaṃ*, *viṇimmiyaṃ*, *vihiaṃ*, *āhiaṃ*, *viraïyaṃ*, *kayaṃ*, *jaṇiyaṃ*. PāiLaNā. 76. Exhausted, dejected, well-settled, departed, powerless, weary, and distressed; agitated, uplifted, lamenting, terrified. Fashioned, constructed, performed, narrated, composed, made, produced.
Know that *ghattaṇa*, *kavaliya*, *asiya*, *vilumpiya*, *vamphiya*, and *khaïya* [denote] eating;
*saccaviya*, *diṭṭha*, *pulaïya*, and *niyacchiya* [denote] seeing;
*nihāliya* [denotes] looking at; *pavvāliya* [denotes] drinking; and *māumbāliya* [denotes] a mass of water. (PāiLaNā 77–78)
Trembling, horripilation, bristling, thrilling, choking,
bursting forth, scattering, casting aside,
abandoning, relinquishing, emitting, spilling, shedding, and flowing forth. (PāiLaNā 79)
*Vēyaḍiyaṃ*, *pajjhuttaṃ*, *khaciyaṃ*, *vicchuriyayaṃ*, and *jaḍiyaṃ*.
*Vōlīṇaṃ*, *vukkantaṃ*, *aïcchiyaṃ*, *vōliyaṃ*, *aïkkantaṃ*, *paḍihatthaṃ*, *uddhumāyaṃ*, *ahirēmaïyaṃ*, and *apphuṇṇaṃ*. (PāiLaNā 80–81)
Shaken, raised up, tossed upward, pulled out, extracted, made to bloom, caused to open, fully blossomed, and fully expanded;
proclaimed, accomplished, prepared, fried, and made known—thus it was explained. (PāiLaNā 82)
*Pavvāya*, *vasuyāya*, *susiya*, and *milāṇattha* [are used] in the sense of "dried up.
*Vicchūḍha*, *ucchitta*, *paṇulliya*, *pilliya*, *galatthiyaya*, *pēḍhāla*, *niyakkala*, and *vaṭṭula* [are used] in the sense of "circular" (*parimaṇḍala*). (PāiLaNā 83–84)
*Ṭiviḍikkiya*, *ciñcilliya*, *ciñcaïya*, *pasāhiya*, *maṇḍiyaya*, *āluṅkhia*, *āliddha*, *chikka*, *chitta*, *parāmusiya*;
*sāmaggiya*, *avayāsiya*, *āliṅgiya*, *uvaūḍha*, *ōsatta*. (PāiLaNā 85)
It smells sweetly, it is fragrant, it shines, it glows, it is beautiful, and it is radiant.
It is always, incessantly, without interruption, at every moment, eternally, constantly, perpetually—cool, refreshing, a shelter, slender, delicate, emaciated, and lean. (PāiLaNā 86–87)
Lalita (graceful), vaggu (charming), mañju (gentle), mañjulaya (delightfully soft), pēsala (excellent), kala (melodious), mahura (sweet), kōmalaya (tender), suhaphaṁsa (pleasant to the touch),
sōmāla (delicate), pēlava (slender), and maüya (soft). Viyaḍa (vast),
viula (abundant), pihula (broad), vitthinna (extensive), vitthaya (expanded), uru (great), and visāla (spacious).
Know that turbid water is like a muddy puddle or a swamp.

(PāiLaNā.89) [The state of] intense, extreme, powerful, and very firm [attachment] is, through the power of delusion, considered to be the ultimate vision, the ultimate happiness, and the ultimate attainment when seen in one's thoughts. (PāiLaNā.90)
Manifest, proclaimed, near, moving along with the body, hidden, dark, discerned, known, understood, awakened to, and realized.
It is dark, sword-like, tranquil, black, complete, and the opposite of white; it is black. (PāiLaNā. 91)
*seya*, *siya*, *valakkha*, *avadāya*, *paṇḍu*, and *dhavala* [mean white].
(PāiLaNā 92) *kavila*, *kavisa*, *piṅga*, *pisaṅgaya*, *piṅgaya*, *kaḍāra*, *aruṇa*, *sōṇa*, *ratta*, *pāḍala*, *āyambira*, and *tamba* [mean reddish-brown or tawny]. (PāiLaNā 93)
I contemplate the names of these mountains—Phasala, Sabala, Sāra, Kimmīra, Cittala, and Bogilla—in the verses of the *Gāhā*. (PāiLaNā.
94) Amarāvatī, Surapurī, Tiviṭṭhaya, and likewise Surālaya are known [as the names of other mountains].
Ālayā, Kubera’s city; the Jina Arhat is the lord of the holy ford (tīrtha).
Kamalā, Śrī, and Lakṣmī; Gajamukha Hēramba is the lord of the Gaṇas.
Ṛkṣa, Uḍu, and Nakṣatra; the Guhyakas are the Yakṣas with auspicious eyes. (PāiLaNā 95–96)

The Nandana grove, the Amarujjāṇa garden, the Golden Mountain, the Divine Mountain Sumeru, the Crystal Mountain Kailāsa, Vihassai (Bṛhaspati), the preceptor of the gods Dhiṣaṇa; the son of Vāsava Jayanta, the daughter of Puloma Śacī, and Indāṇī (Indrāṇī). PāiLaNā. 97.
Airāvaṇa, Suragaja, Vidyut, Sītāmaṇi, and Taḍī;
Asani, Vajra, Kulisa, Surāuha, and the bow of the gods (Tridaśacāpa);
Indradhanu, Aṅgāraka, Bhauma, Uśanas, Śukra, and Daityaguru.
The world, the universe, the people, the lord of men, the ruler, the sovereign, the king;
a friend, a companion, a playmate; a minister, a counselor, and an official;
a pupil, a disciple, a cheat, a juggler, and a deceiver. (PāiLaNā. 100)
The wealthy, the noble, the rich, kinsmen, relatives, and those with protectors;
the Brahmin, the giver, the donor, limbs, Nandana, sons, children, those born of noble lineage, the dependent, the servant, and the retainer. (PāiLaNā.101–102)
The non-attendants are heavy, lowly, and others who are commoners;
they are leaders, chariot-makers, increasers, calves, and cowherds.
The villages consist of umbrellas and grain; there are village chiefs, enjoyers, and village lords.

The potter and the wheelwright, the cowherd, the cattle-tender, and the gova; the shopkeeper, the merchant, the liquor-seller, and likewise the wanderer; the fisherman, the fowler, the sailor, and the slave. (PāiLaNā 104–105)
The beggar, the one who carries a load, the flower-gatherer, the one who gathers flowers, the pillar, the drop, the small amount, the dwarf, and the hunchback;
the weeper, the lame woman, the mute, the one who is silent, and the one who remains quiet. (PāiLaNā 106)

The transformation of age is old age; she is an aged woman, worn out and past her youth. (PāiLaNā.107) A golden palace, the moon’s mansion, a garland, likewise a mother, a female friend, a paternal aunt, another's property, another's will, renowned, famous, and manifest. (PāiLaNā.108)
The nails, the teeth, the claws, the hair of the head, the curls, the hair of the body,
the tail-hairs, the feet, the steps, the soles, the shoulders,
as well as the breasts, the hips; the forearms, the hands, the palms, the skin, the antelope-skin, the hide, and the leather.
*Daśanā*, *rayaṇā*, *dantā*; *sīrōharā*, *kandharā*, *gīvā*.
*Vayaṇaṃ*, *muhaṃ*, *āṇaṇaṃ*; *acchī*, *nayaṇaṃ*, *lōyaṇaṃ*; *nittaṃ*, *nāsā*, *ghāṇaṃ*, *ghōṇā*; *sīsaṃ*, *siraṃ*, *uttamaṅgaṃ*. (PāiLaNā.110–111)

The forehead (*bhāla*), the brow (*aliya*), the temple (*niḍāla*), the beard (*maṁsu*), the chin (*khaḍḍa*), the cheek (*māsurī*), the breast (*kucca*), the belly (*udara*), the abdomen (*jaḍhara*), the navel (*tunda*), tears (*bappha*), and sweat (*bāhī*) are the water of the eyes (*nayaṇajala*). The sense-organ (*indriya*), the faculty (*akkha*), the instrument (*karaṇa*), radiance (*chāyā*), luster (*kantī*), skin (*chavī*), and beauty (*lāyanna*). PāiLaNā.112–113ab.
Urine, pus, flesh, broth, blood, and gore;
the nasal cavity, the nose, the veins, excrement, feces, and evacuation;
a mark, a brand, a sign, sweat, moisture, and perspiration. (Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā 113–114)
A waistband, a girdle, a belt, a sash, a string of pearls, a necklace, a crown, a diadem, and a crest-jewel;
a veil, a ring, an ornament, a decoration, and an embellishment. (PāiLaNā. 115)
*vinnāsa* (destruction), *vicchitti* (ornamentation), *kannāṃsa* (ear-lobe), and *talavatta* (palm-leaf fan);
*talima* (carpet), *tappa* (bed-covering), *sayaṇa* (bed), *aṅgarāga* (unguent for the limbs), and *vilēvaṇa* (ointment);
*caccā* (a type of garment), *bāullī* (a doll), *puttaliyā* (a small doll), *vivaṇī* (market-street), as well as *āvaṇa* (shop) and *haṭṭha* (market). (PāiLaNā 116–117)
Umbrellas, water-vessels, swans, anklets, and foot-ornaments;
thrones, lion-thrones, head-dresses, and turbans; windows, lattices, mirrors, and looking-glasses. (Pāi La Nā 118)
Vēruliya (cat's-eye), vēḍujja (lapis lazuli), kalahoya (onyx), ruppaya (silver), and rayaya (crystal).
Sōvīra (sour gruel), āranāla (fermented rice water), sneha (oil/fat), pimma (affection), rasa (flavor), and anurāga (passion).
Pīṭha (seat), viṭṭhara (bedding), āsana (throne), ahirōhaṇiyā (staircase), and nissēṇī (ladder).
*Sīra* is a plough; *naṅgala* is a ploughshare; *āuha* is a weapon; *attha* is a missile;
*māḍhī* is a shield; *kavaya* is breastplate armor; *asimuṭṭhī* is a sword-hilt; *pāliyā* is a spear; *charū* is a dagger.
*Cakka* refers to wheels; *rahaṅga* refers to chariot parts; *sittha* is a living being; *guṇa* is a string; *paḍa* is a cloth. (PāiLaNā 121)
*Talima* and *paṭṭha* are [synonyms for] a surface; *talaṃ* is [the same as] *vivañciyā*. *Vallai* and *vīṇā* are [synonyms for] a lute. (PāiLaNā.

122) *Milk* (*chīra*), *paya*, and *duddha* are [synonyms for] milk; *sisira*, *dahiya*, *ciraḍḍhihilla*, and *ajja* are [synonyms for] curd; *sappi*, *ghaya*, *amaya*, *suhā*, and *pīūsa* are [synonyms for] clarified butter (*ghṛta*). (PāiLaNā. 123)
The pigeon, the woodpecker, the sparrow, the house-bell (the common quail), the sparrow-hawk, the blue jay,
the female partridge, the *saüṇī*, the *bhiṅghārī*, the cricket, the *cīrī*, the cakravāka, the ruddy goose,
the *kayavā* (the lapwing), the cock, and the *tambasihā* (the peacock). — Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā 124.
A female swan is called *varalā*, a male swan is *kaṇaïlla*, and a parrot is *pūsa*.
A vulture has a deep voice (*gahara-vaō*). A deer is *sāraṅga* or *cāyaya*, and a peacock is *bappīha*.
Its feathers are *piccha* or *pehuṇa*, and its nest is *nīḍa*, *niḍḍa*, or *kulāya*. (Pāia-lacchī-nāmamālā 125–126)
The boar is *kiḍī*, the wild boar is *varāhō*, the rhinoceros is *bhulluṅkī*, and the *bhasuyā* is the great-noised [elephant].
The young elephant is *kalaho*, the male elephant is *hatthī*, the female elephant is *karēṇuyā*, and the mate of the *gayavahū* is the *kariṇī*.
The *karimayarō* is the water-elephant; the *kaḍuyālā* and *kumbarā* are the small fish.
The *ricchō*, the *acchahallō*, the tail, the hair, and the scales;
the palate, the whirlpool, the crab, the *kuruvillayā*, and the *kakkaḍayā*;
the oyster, the *chiñchōlī*, the mud, the *jambālō*, the *khañjaṇō*, and the mire. (PāiLaNā. 128–129)
A well that is not dug and one that is dug, the Mehalakannā river and the Narmadā;
the Rēvā river, a pond, a vast marshy plain, a lotus pool, a long tank, and a lake; a sprout, a rampart, and a bank; and the *sālūra*, the *daddura*, and the *maṇḍukka* frogs.
A water-wheel (*arahaṭṭha*), a pot being fashioned (*ghaḍijanta*), a field for sowing (*kēyāra*), and the act of sowing (*vappa*).

A well (*nāruṭṭha*), a small pond (*kūsāra*), irrigation channels (*ōhārā*), tortoises (*kamaḍhaka*), marshes (*kachchahā*), turtles (*kummā*), the Goyāvarī river, the Gōlā river, foam (*ḍiṇḍīra*), a flower (*pupphaya*), and froth (*phēṇa*). (Pāia-lacchi-nāmamālā 131–132)
The bank, the ox, the stone, the shore, the crossing of a river, thirst, craving, and parching; the hidden, the ungraspable, and the deep;
the reeds, the slender streams, the moss, the water-weed, and the mud. (Pāi La Nā 133)
*Doṇī*, *kuṭṭhimbā*, *kōṭumbhō*, and *jalakarapphālō* [are synonyms for a certain type of vessel]. (PāiLaNā.
134) *Jālā*, *accīo*, *sihāu*, *addharā*, *sattatantuṇō*, *jannā*, *pāyā*, *kaḍayā*, *sāṇū*, *kantāraṁ*, *kāṇaṇaṁ*, and *rannaṁ* [are synonyms for forest]. (PāiLaNā. 135)
Bud, sprout, peak, summit, branch, twig, small branch, leaf, stalk, creeper, flower, blossom, and fruit;
*kusumaraya*, *makaranda* (honey), pollen, dust, *rajas*, and *parāga*. (PāiLaNā 136)

The *kōsī*, *samī*, *simbā*, *dalaṃ*, *palāsaṃ*, *chayaṃ*, and *pattaṃ*; the bark (*challī*), the inner bark (*tayā*), the shoots (*cuḍuppaṃ*), the young sprouts (*kisilāiṃ*), the tender leaves (*pallavā*), and the new foliage (*pavālā*); as well as *tiṅicchī*, *kamalaraō*, *malaō*, *ujjāṇaṃ*, and *ārāmō*. PāiLaNā.137–138.

Water-vessels, basins, *tōmara-guṇḍī*, and *mañjarī-guṇḍī*; creepers, climbing plants, shrubs, clusters, and bunches; leafy abundance, *pattala*, *āmēlā*, *cubbhalā*, and *sēharaya*. —Pāiā Laṅkānāma, 139.1–2.
A wreath, a garland, a string; sounding, tinkling, jingling.
(PāiLaNā.140) Ummāla, nimmalla, guvila, kalila, and vallara;
a thicket, a forest fire, a conflagration, a fire in a grove, a fire in a thicket, a brushfire. (PāiLaNā.141)
A bamboo pole, a forest-clearing, a guard, a cow-pen, a settlement, a threshing floor, straw, deception, instruction, destruction, and falsehood;
a pillar, a stone slab, a creeper, a piece cut by a chisel, a fish, and a broken edge. (Pāia-lakṣaṇa 142)
Ripe, fully matured, and transformed: *ikkhu*, *ucchū*, and the sugarcane field (*ucchuvaṇa*).
Bamboo (*vaṃsa*), reed (*vēṇu*), cane (*vēlu*), *vañjula*, *vēḍasa*, and *vāṇīra*;
likewise *jāsuyaṇa*, *javā*, *phaliṇī*, *piyamā*, and *piyaṅgu*.
Sindola, khajjūra, ambā, māyanda, cūta, sahakāra, taravaṭṭa, pāmāḍa, ambiliyā, ciñciṇī, and ciñcā;
kohaliyā, kōhaṇḍī, baruva, sāmuṇḍua, and bhamāsa. (PāiLaNā 145)
Hayamāra, kaṇavīra, sulasā, and likewise mañjuyā and tulasī; [these are the fragrant plants].
Madaṇāhi, kastūrī, malayaruha, candana, and ikkaṅga;
ghanasāra, kappūra, āmōa, parimala, and gandha [are the names for various perfumes].
Bimbāya, bhallāya, pāyayīya, vayalī, mayālī, kaṇṭulla, kaṅkōḍa, mālūra, sirihala, billa;
amilāṇa, koraṇṭa, nalaya, lāmañjaya, and usīra. (PāiLaNā 148)
Punnāga, suravannī, bhisiṇī, naliṇī, and kamaliṇī.
(PāiLaNā.149) Suragova, indova, kōliyaya, unnanāha, akkaḍaya, majjārī, birālī, rāsaha, gaddaha, and khara. (PāiLaNā.150)
The *bhōū*, *phaḍa*, *phaṇattha*, *kuṇḍulluya*, *kōsiyā*, *ulūya*, *rōmantha*, *uggāla*, *ukkhā*, *vasaha*, and *vacchaṇā*;
the *jantu*, *satta*, *bhūya*, *kōlhuya*, *jaṃbua*, and *gomāu*. (PāiLaNā. 151)
A hut, a house of feeling, a village, a market town, a hamlet, and a city.
(PāiLaNā.152) A swing, a rope, a crackling sound, a small bell, a fire of dung, a spread of straw, a bed-covering, a clod of earth, a lump of earth, and a ball of earth.
(PāiLaNā.153)
The bridegroom is the obstacle; she is intent on him, her mind absorbed in him, and desirous of him alone.
Her eyes are like lamps, and her thighs are the enemies of those lamps.
[She is] the wood, the fuel, the timber, the provision, the travel-rations, and the necessary equipment. (PāiLaNā. 154)
*Bhāva*, *vatthu*, and *payattha* mean "state" or "thing"; *khujja* means "crooked," and *kuḍilla* means "curved.
(PāiLaNā 155) *Indamaha* and *kōmāra* refer to festivals; *kōuya* and *kuḍḍa* refer to curiosity (*kōuhalla*).
*Surahī* is honey, *mahū* is spring (*vasanta*), and *vāsāratta* is the rainy season (*ghaṇasamaō*). (PāiLaNā 156)
Illusion, deceit, falsehood, great days, days, days;
frost, snow, ice, masses of clouds, dark earth; a corpse, a skeleton, a carcass, a cremation ground, a forest of ancestors, and a cemetery.
Embers, charcoal, eating, likewise eating again, avoidance; PāiLaNā.158.
Receiving instruction, newness, obstacles, hindrances, impediments, and distress; incapacity, happiness, great joy, and delight; PāiLaNā.159.
It is called *ugghāya*, *ārambha*, *saṅkhēva*, *saṅgaha*, and *samāsa*;
it is eternal (*nicca*), constant (*niyaya*), permanent (*sāsaya*), without food (*avvāhāra*), and without speech (*aṇālavaya*).
It is also designated by the names *vāvaḍayā*, *akkhaṇiyā*, *sannā*, *gutta*, and *ahiḍāṇa*. (PāiLaNā 160)
*Attī*, *viyaṇā*, *pīḍā*, *saṃrambha*, *amarisa*, and *mannu*. (PāiLaNā.
161) *Muḷlāiṃ*, *vēyaṇāiṃ*, *paccaggaṃ*, *ahiṇavaṃ*, *ca*, *sajjukkaṃ*, *āvāō*, *pamuhaṃ*, *muraḥ*, *hēlā*, *aṇāyaraḥ*, and *rīḍhā*. (PāiLaNā. 162)
Know *karamba*, *tottaḍi*, *avaratta*, *anusaya*, *anutāva*,
*kūra*, *caṇḍa*, *ōyaṇa*, *ōṇaya*, *ōyatta*, and *ōmattha*. [PāiLaNā 163] Also *thāma*, *sāra*, *bala*, *thēva*, *lēsa*, *lava*, *kalā*, and *mattā*.
Similarity, having the same head, lack of faith, discontent, and longing;
from this point forward, as well as from here on, agitation, conduct, effort, deliberation, shame, displeasure, wonder, marvel, and astonishment. (PāiLaNā 164–165)
Length, extension, swiftness, fickleness, unsteady, tremulous, and so forth—these are merely synonyms for sport (*kēlī*), and nothing else; nor is there any jesting. *PāiLaNā*.
166: *pala* (moment), destruction, ruin, merit, good deed, and fortune.
*Hittha*, *viliya*, *lajjiya*, *atthāṇī*, as well as *sahā* and *parisā*.
(PāiLaNā.167) *Unnāha*, *ussēha*, *vikkhambha*, *vitthara*, and *pariṇāha*;
*parirambhaṇa*, *avaruṇḍaṇa*, *āmōa*, *paharisa*, and *tōsa*. (PāiLaNā.168)
The dance, the rhythmic movement, the successive sequences, the series, the protection,
the city-guard, the practice, the cultivation of qualities, the fitness, attentiveness, one-pointedness of mind,
and the daily tasks performed day by day— these constitute the daily routine. (PāiLaNā 169)
*Ōluggō*, *nitthāmō*, *dujjāyaṃ*, *āvayā*, *vasaṇaṃ*.
*Chuṭṭaṃ*, *maḍahaṃ*, *lahuyaṃ*, *rapphā*, *vammīya-vāmalūrā*,
and *pāyālaṃ*, *rasāyalaṃ*, *āulaṃ*, *āhitthaṃ*, *uppitthaṃ*.
*Vēsa*, *ahō*, *manthāṇa*, *sīluṭṭa*, *cibbhiḍa*, and *vāluṅka*;
*kumbha*, *kuḍa*, *kalasa*, *piḍhara*, *ḍhamara*, and *kōlamba*.
*Kuḍila*, *vaṅka*, *bhaṅgura*, *āēsa*, *sāsana*, and *niddēsa*.
Quickly, swiftly, rapidly; clever, reaching the limit, going to the end.
(PāiLaNā.173) Long, very long, extended; crooked, straight, and diligent;
fit, skillful, and clever; firm, forceful, and violent; by force, by compulsion. (PāiLaNā.174)

*Paüṇaṃ*, *nirāyaṃ*, *ujjuyaṃ*, *ōlaïyaṃ*, *parihiyaṃ*, *piṇaddhaṃ*, and *avarillaṃ* refer to the upper garment (*uttarijja*). *Uyaṭṭhī* is the waist-knot (*nīvī*). *Duddhiyaṃ*, *alābu*, *tumbaṃ*, *nibandhaṇaṃ*, *kāraṇaṃ*, and *niyāṇaṃ* are synonyms for cause. (PāiLaNā. 175)
*vilaō* (ruin), *sūratthamaṇaṁ* (loss of courage), *saṅkhōhō* (agitation), *sambhamō* (confusion), *tāsō* (terror).

*ullūriyam* (uprooted), *ukkaḍiyaṁ* (dragged out), *jaṅghiyamōsiṅghiyaṁ* (sniffed at the heels), *ca* (and), *agghāyaṁ* (smelled), *nivviṭṭhaṁ* (entered), *uvahuttaṁ* (turned toward), *tirōhiyaṁ* (hidden), *pihiyam* (covered), *antariyaṁ* (interposed). PāiLaNā 176–177.
Uddāliya, acchinna, akkhitta, añchiya, kaḍḍhiyaya, pannāḍiyaya, parihaṭṭhiya, osariya, osakka; utthalliya, ucchaliya, pacchāiya, nūmiyā, vaiyā. (PāiLaNā 178)
*Niddhāḍiyaṃ*, *nīṇiyaṃ*, *ohīraṃtaṃ*, and *sīyaṃtaṃ*;
*unnāliyaṃ*, *unnāmiyaṃ*, *uvagayaṃ*, *uvasappiyaṃ*, and *allīṇaṃ*; *cuṇṇaïyaṃ*, *cunnāhayaṃ*, *ucciḍimaṃ*, *mukkaṃ*, and *ajjāyaṃ*. (PāiLaNā. 179–180)
Torn upward, puffed up, burst open, split apart, shattered, rolled up,
crushed, withered, weak, decayed, shattered to pieces, pulverized, tossed about, struck down, and cast away. (PāiLaNā.181)
Know *murumuriya* (murmuring), *tūruiya* (hurrying), *unnuiya* (rising up), *bhukkiya* (eating).

*Avaciyam* (gathering down), *ucciṇiyatthe* (picking up), *taḍiyam* (beaten), *taḍḍaviyayam* (crushed), *viralliyayam* (spread out), *uvvamiyam* (vomited), *uggiliyam* (spit out), *chuhāiyam* (hungry), *bhukkhiyam* (eaten), and *chāyam* (shadow). — Paiyalacchināmamālā 182–183.
Struck, shaken, heard, listened to, perceived, sufficient, abundant, offered, given, brought near;
doubtful, suspected, churned, searched, wandered over the meaning. (PāiLaNā.184)
Visible, sent away, high, bitter, and thirsting;
*raṅkhōlira*, *pahōlira*, *uvvella*, *pasariya*, *payalla*, *saṅkōḍiya*, *niuñciya*, *uttējiya*, and *tōraviya*. (PāiLaNā.185–186)
Overflowing, leaking, pouring out, deceiving, delaying, spilling, adding, lightening, deluding, weighing; promised, agreed upon, given away, exchanged, and destroyed. (PāiLaNā. 187)
Likewise, *aisaiya*, *visesiya*, *ummuṭṭha*, *puñchiya*, and *phusiya*;
*vikkhittaya*, *païṇṇa*, *khitta*, *nigghattiya*, and *āiddha*;
*uggāhiya*, *uccāliya*, *aṅkusaïya*, and *aṅkusāyāra*. (PāiLaNā 188–189)
Rushed upon, attacked, seized, oppressed, defeated, forgotten, lost, hurriedly moved, trembling, quivering; fallen, slipped away, missed, abandoned, disregarded, and utterly cast aside. (PāiLaNā 190)
Lamented, wailed, scattered, churned, and crushed;
shaken down, released, covered, and dusted, as well as sprinkled with dust; reviled, spat upon, filled up, overturned, and cast away. (PāiLaNā 191–192)

That which has been entered, descended into, sought, searched for, investigated, tasted, smelled, deposited, placed, stored, filled, obtained, remembered, suspected, cast down, and wiped away. (PāiLaNā.
*Nisuḍhiyam*, *akkantabharōṇayam*, *ubbhaḍavēsaṁ*, and *uvvivvaṁ*;
*samuhāgayam*, *ōsariyaṁ*, *binduiyaṁ*, *kaṇaïyaṁ*, *kaṇāyaṇṇaṁ*, *viramāliyaṁ*, *vihīriyam*, *ōrāliyayaṁ*, and *māliyayaṁ*. (PāiLaNā. 194–195)
Thinned out, scraped, pared, split, pierced, flown upward, soared, distressed, exhausted, led astray, dragged out, poured out, bound, fettered, and shackled. (PāiLaNā. 196)
It was woven with threads, dyed with safflower, highly honored, free from impurities, thick, well-arranged, split, bordered, and darkened like collyrium;
it was blackened, encircled, and completely surrounded. (PāiLaNā 197–198)
Encircled, surrounded, covered, and overcast;
approached, settled, and hidden; crushed by the emission of fragrance;
emerged, fashioned, displayed, shown, and revealed. (PāiLaNā. 199)
Tikkhāliyaṃ, nisāyaṃ, puluṭṭhayaṃ, paüliyaṃ, daḍḍhaṃ;
palhatthiyaṃ, ullaṇḍiyaṃ, ucchuṇṇaṃ, maddiyaṃ, and niddaliyaṃ; pēsaviyaṃ, paṭṭhaviyaṃ, ghaḍiyaṃ, laggaṃ, and saṃsattaṃ. (PāiLaNā.200–201)
Sleep is shaken off, one is able to leave [it], one crosses over, and one reaches the further shore;
I shall now explain each of these names individually.
*Karaḍā* refers to the temples of an elephant; *ālāṇa* is the pillar for binding an elephant.
The Karibandhana is declared [to be the first]; Upaya, Vāraṇamaya, and Dāna [are the next].
Know that Rava, Alasa, Kalamañjula, Ōralli, Madhuradīhara, and Suivirasa are Gaddabha; and Gaggara is that which is faltering in the throat. (PāiLaNā. 203–204)
Know that it is the *ōūla*, the *pālamba*, the *hariyandaṇa*, the *amaracandaṇa*, the *jāṇa*, the *jaccaturaṅga*, the *bhāyala*, the *āyāvalaya*, and the *aruṇatāva*.
It is the *sīmantiya*, the *duhāviya*, the final, the last, the unrestrained, and the lofty. (PāiLaNā.205)
Vāyaṇaya, pahēṇaya, iṅgālī, and ucchugaṇḍīrī.
(PāiLaNā.206) Viśaḍha, viśama, viyalia, uccatta, kattiyāsina, sarao, sisira, phagguṇamāha, hēmanta, posa, and aggasiro. (PāiLaNā.207)

*Duppariyalla* (difficult to grasp), *asakka* (impossible), *pukkāō* (a type of grass), *aliyapōrusa* (false heroism), *ālāvā* (talk), *pañjāya* (arrangement), *piṇḍalaïya* (a type of tree), *muū* (a type of tree), *riū* (enemy), *cottaō* (a type of tree), *tottō* (a goad);
*uvayārō* (service), *pupphabalī* (flower offering), *kusumaṅkāliñjaṇīe* (a type of plant), *tāvicchaṁ* (a type of tree). — PāiLaNā. 208.
Javasa is grass; gavitta is *ulava*; vīraṇa is *ōlāva*; and seṇa is a heap. (PāiLaNā.209) Agga is the shoulder;
khaṇḍha is the trunk; aṇiya is a footman; pāḍuccī is the dust raised by the bodies of horses;
garala and visa are poison; visāṇa and siṅga are horn; and rajjū and varattā are rope. (PāiLaNā.210)
*Jagala*, *piṅgalasara*, *biṇṭhasurā*, *piṭṭhakhaüriyā*, *maïrā*, *hijja*, *kalla*, *nivva*, *paḍala*, *kāhilliyā*, and *tavaa* denote wine.
*Aṇurōha*, *dakkhiṇṇa*, *laggaṇa*, *paḍihuā*, *dara*, and *addha* denote a small portion. —PāiLaNā 211.
That cloth which is placed upon Ānanda is called the "merit-cloth" (puṇṇavatta).
[PāiLaNā.212] That which is sewn, gathered, enjoyed, honored, and beautiful—the hall situated above the palace—is called the "moon-hall" (candasālā). [PāiLaNā.213]
That which is overflowing, filled with extraordinary power, spread out, expanded, and abandoned—[that] face, [which is] a stream of anger, is called *thuḍaṅkiyaya*. (PāiLaNā.
